L17: # MCP Safety Warden [Update 1]
L18: 
L19: 【4†server】
L20: 
L21: 【5†Image: media poster†external-preview.redd.it】
L22: 
L23: Hi all! A couple of days ago I launched MCP Safety Warden, a security proxy for MCP servers. It has already hit over ~2k downloads on PyPI :)
L24: 
L25: Really appreciate everyone who tested it out and shared feedback.
L26: 
L27: Based on the initial feedback, here are the major updates:
L28: 
L29:   1. Improved documentation
L30:   2. Source code analysis At launch, the scanner could only infer risk from tool names and descriptions. It can now audit any public MCP server directly from its GitHub repo before you even register or connect it. This includes entropy detection, AST analysis, description mismatch checks, and more. If the server is registered on the proxy, MCP Safety Warden can go further with pen-test-style live probing on top of the static analysis.
L31:   3. Drift detection MCP servers change over time. Tool removal, parameter changes, description rewrites, any of these can break your agent or quietly introduce a new attack surface. MCP Safety Warden can now detect these drifts once your server is registered. And this happens during tool calls as well!
L32: 
L33: Feel free to test it out, and please do share any feedback!

L72: drift detection on live tool calls is the feature that matters most here — silent description rewrites are exactly how you'd execute a prompt injection attack post-install, and most people have no visibility into that happening. the AST analysis catching description mismatches is solid too; a tool that says 'read file' but spawns a subprocess is a classic supply chain red flag. curious whether the live probing does any output fuzzing or just static comparison against the registered baseline.
